chunks: 1692 - And he, peace be upon him, said to al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar:

“O Mufaḍḍal, if you wish to know whether a man is wretched or fortunate, then look at his kindness and to whom he gives it. If he gives it to one who deserves it, then know that he is upon good. And if he gives it to one other than its people, then know that he has no good with Allah, the Exalted.”

key_terms.أَهْلُهُ: Those who are worthy or deserving of it.
key_terms.سَعِيدٌ: Fortunate; one marked by felicity and goodness.
key_terms.شَقِيٌّ: Wretched; one marked by misery or ill fate.
key_terms.مَعْرُوفِهِ: His kindness or recognized good deed.

ai.seo_question: How can one tell whether a person is truly fortunate or wretched according to Imam عليه السلام?
ai.summary: The Imam عليه السلام teaches that a person's true state is recognized by where he directs his acts of goodness. Properly placed kindness is a sign of goodness, while misdirected favor indicates a lack of true good before Allah, the Exalted.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1692 - Imam (as) said to Al-Mufaddal ibn Umar:

"O Mufaddal, if you wish to know whether a person is fortunate or wretched, observe to whom he directs his kindness. If he extends it to those who are deserving, then know that he is inclined toward goodness. But if he extends it to those who are undeserving, then know that he has no share of goodness with Allah (swt), the Exalted."
